newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran launches new wargames, U.S. to defend Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran launches new wargames, U.S. to defend Gulf.

text.p: Thousands of Iranian air and naval forces launched new wargames in the Gulf on Sunday and a top U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz against any Iranian threat.
Some 4,000 men backed by destroyers, helicopter gunships and fighters began six days of exercises stretching the length of the Gulf.
The exercises, codenamed Salman-e Fateh after a Persian companion of the Prophet Mohammad, are to enhance combat readiness and tactics against a mock enemy, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.
In Bahrain, headquarters of the U.S. Fifth Fleet, General Binford Peay, Commander-in-Chief of the U.S. Central Command, said the United States would ensure the strait stayed open.

"Access to the strait is very important, not just to the United States of America, but it is vitally important for the entire world," Peay said on Saturday when asked about an Iranian threat to close the narrow entrance to the Gulf if attacked by Washington.
His remarks were released by the U.S. embassy in Manama on Sunday.

The commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, Major-General Mohsen Rezaei, said after Iran's biggest wargames last month: "We can keep the Strait of Hormuz open...but if we want to, we shall close this strait to anyone who is an obstacle to security in the region and keep it open for our friends and the Moslems."

The 55 km (35 miles) wide strait is guarded by Iran on its northern shore and the Gulf Arab sultanate of Oman on the south. About 15 million barrels of oil -- half the world's exports -- pass through each day to customers in Asia, Europe and North America.
"The United States will be a major player in ensuring these straits remain open," Peay said. The United States keeps about 20 warships in the Gulf.
"Our navy is the very best in the world...I can assure you that we are going to keep the straits open and no country should pose that kind of aggression in this very important region," Peay added.

Iran's new wargames, stretching from the strait to the northern Gulf, were the latest mock battles highlighting the Islamic republic's activity in the Gulf. Ground, naval and air units of Iran's Revolutionary Guards last month staged mock battles.

Gulf Arab states have expressed alarm at an Iranian military buildup despite Tehran's assurances it is defensive. They have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge denied by Tehran.

Tehran has repeatedly denied U.S. allegations it sponsors international terrorism and accuses Washington of stoking regional tensions in order to sell billions of dollars of weapons to its Gulf Arab allies.
